translations.text: The angel of the Lord answered, saying, “Lord Almighty, how long will you withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you have neglected for seventy years now?”
And the Lord Almighty answered the angel who was speaking within me, addressing him with kind words and comforting words.
And the angel who was speaking within me said to me, “Cry out, saying: ‘This is what the Lord Almighty says: I have been deeply jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.’
“‘And I am intensely angry with the nations that rose up together against you, because I was only a little angry, but they rose up to do evil.’”

Therefore, this is what the Lord says: “I will return to Jerusalem with compassion, and my house will be rebuilt in it,” says the Lord Almighty, “and a measuring line will again be stretched out over Jerusalem.”
And the angel who spoke within me said to me, “Cry out, saying: ‘The cities will again overflow with good things, and the Lord will again have mercy on Zion and love Jerusalem.’”
And I raised my eyes and saw four horns.
He said to the angel who was speaking within me, “What are these?” And he said to me, “These are the ones that scattered Judah and the [?].”
“Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, for look, I am coming to live among you,” says the Lord.
And many nations will run to the Lord on that day and become his people, and they will live among you. And you will know that the Lord Almighty is the one who sent me to you.
And the Lord will cause Judah to inherit in his midst, on the holy land, and he will again love [?].
Let all flesh fear before the Lord, because he has risen from his holy clouds.
And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and the devil was standing at his right side to oppose him.
And the Lord said to the devil, “May the Lord rebuke you, the one who chose [?]. And was this man not like a torch snatched from the fire?”
And Joshua was wearing filthy clothes as he stood before the angel of the Lord.
And he answered those standing before him, saying, “Strip him of the filthy clothes.” And he said to him, “Look, I have taken away your sins.”

And he said, “Put a full-length robe on him, and place a headband on him and a clean turban on his head.” And they placed the clean turban on his head and dressed him in clothes, while the angel of the Lord stood there.
And the angel of the Lord testified to Joshua, saying:

“This is what the Lord Almighty says: If you walk in my ways and take care to follow my commands, you will be in charge of my house. And if you guard my courtyard, I will give you those who will be among these who stand here.”
“Listen, then, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men who receive signs. Look, I will bring a rising upon my servant.”
“For the stone that I placed before Joshua—on that one stone are seven eyes. And look, I will dig a pit,” says the Lord Almighty, “and I will overcome all the injustice of that land in a single day.”
“On that day,” says the Lord Almighty, “each of you will invite his neighbor under his vine and under his fig tree.”
And the angel who was speaking within me returned and woke me, as a person is awakened from sleep.
He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I looked, and there was a lampstand entirely of gold, with its lamp on top of it. There were seven lamps on it and seven channels for the lamps on it.”
And there were two olive trees above it, one on the right of its lamp and one on its left.
And I answered the angel who was speaking within me, saying, “What are these?”
He said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
He answered me, saying, “This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by great power or by great strength, but by my [?],’ says the Lord Almighty.”
Who are you, you great mountain before Zerubbabel, to be made level before him? And I will bring out the stone of the inheritance, its grace equal to its grace.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“The hands of Zerubbabel laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it. And you will know that the Lord Almighty sent me to you.”
“Who has despised you for a few days? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in Zerubbabel’s hand. These are the seven eyes of the Lord that look over the whole earth.”
And I answered, saying, “What are these two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”
I asked him again a second time, saying to him, “What are these two olive branches in the hands of the two golden spouts that pour out and bring up the golden ladles?”
He said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
He said to me, “These are the two sons of the oil tree, standing before the Lord of the whole earth.”
And I looked up and saw a flying sickle.
He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.”
He said to me, “This is the curse going out over the whole earth, because every thief will be punished by it with death, and everyone who swears falsely will also be punished by it with death.”

“And I will send it out,” says the Lord Almighty, “and it will enter the thief’s house and the house of the person who swears falsely by my name to do wrong. It will remain in the middle of his house and destroy it, along with its timbers and stones.”
And the angel who spoke within me came out and said to me, “Look up and see what is coming out.”
I said, “What is it, my lord?” He said to me, “This is the measuring basket coming out, and this is their wrongdoing throughout the whole earth.”
And there was a lump of lead being lifted up, and there was a woman sitting in the middle of the measuring basket.
And he said, “This is lawlessness.” And she threw her into the middle of the measuring basket, and she threw the lead stone into its opening.
I looked up and saw two women coming out, with [?] in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a hoopoe, and they lifted the measuring basket up between the earth and the sky.
I said to the angel who spoke within me, “Where will these women take the measuring basket?”
He said to me, “To build for it [?]”
And in the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chislev.
Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king will come to you. He is righteous and brings salvation. He is gentle, riding on a beast of burden and a young foal.

And he will destroy chariots from Ephraim and horses from Jerusalem. They will destroy the battle bow, along with a multitude, while he speaks peace to the nations. His authority will extend from the sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.
And you, through the blood of your covenant, have sent your prisoners out of a pit with no water in it.
Return to a stronghold, prisoners of hope! And in place of the single day of your exile, I will repay you double.
“For, Judah, I have bent you for myself as a bow; I have filled Ephraim. And I will raise up your sons, Zion, against the sons of [?], and I will make them strong like a warrior’s sword.”
And the Lord will come down upon them, and his arrow will go out like lightning, and the Lord God will sound a great trumpet.
And I will say to them, “If it seems good to you, give me my wages and pay them; otherwise, refuse.” And they paid me my wages, thirty pieces of silver.

And the Lord said to me, “Throw it into the smelting furnace, so that I may test whether it is sound, in the way they tested it.” And I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the smelting furnace in the house of the Lord …
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will increase, like the cutting down of a pomegranate grove that is being cut down in the plain.
And the land will mourn, each family separately: the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves.
The family of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Simeon by itself, and their wives by themselves.
All the families that remain, each separately, and their wives separately.
And on that day every place that is opened will become a house of David, and a spring will be opened for the house of David and those who live in Jerusalem.
And on that day, says the Lord of Hosts, “I will remove the name of the idols from the land, and they will not return.”

And if anyone prophesies again, his father and his mother who gave birth to him will say to him, “You will not live, because you have spoken lies in the name of the Lord.” And his father and his mother who gave birth to him will bind him when he prophesies.
And on that day the prophets will each be ashamed of their visions when they prophesy, and they will put on skins because they have lied.
And he will say, “I am not a prophet, because a man fathered me and taught me from my childhood.”
And I will say to him, “What are these wounds between your hands?” And he will say to me, “These are the wounds they gave me in the house of my beloved.”

“Sword, rise against the shepherd and against the man who is his fellow citizen,” says the Lord Almighty. “Strike the shepherd, and let the sheep be scattered. And I will bring my hand against the little shepherds.”
And throughout the whole land, says the Lord, two parts will perish and disappear, but a third will remain in it.

“And I will bring the third through fire and refine them as silver is refined, and I will test them as gold is tested. He will call on my name, and I will listen to him. I will say, ‘This is my people,’ and he will say, ‘You are the Lord my God.’”
Look, a day of the Lord is coming, and the plunder will be divided within you.

And I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for war. They will capture the city and plunder the houses, and the women will be raped. Half the people of the city will go into captivity, but the rest of the people will not be destroyed from the city.
And the Lord will go out and fight against those nations, as in the days when he fought on the day of battle.
And his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which faces Jerusalem on the east.
And the Lord my God will come, with all the holy ones with him.
And on that day there will be no light, and there will be cold and frost in a single day.
And that day is known to the Lord. It is neither day nor night, and at evening light will shine.
And on that day living light will come out of Jerusalem, half of it toward the first sea and the other half toward the last sea. It will be this way in summer and spring.
And the Lord will be king

over the whole land and the wilderness, from Gabel to Hermon, south of Jerusalem. But Ramah will remain in its inhabited place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the First Gate and the Corner Gate, and from the tower of Ameel to the king’s winepresses.
And they will live in it and will no longer be under a curse, and [?] will be inhabited securely [?].
